decisions.statement: The hold is one file named for the thing being put up.
The hold sits under the folder every worktree of the checkout shares.
Taking the hold is one create that fails where the hold is there.
The hold names the process holding it and the moment that process started.
A hold a live process keeps refuses the second deploy rather than waiting on it.
A hold left by a process that is gone is taken rather than refused.
A refusal names the thing, the process holding it and how long that hold has been there.
The hold is released however the deploy inside it ends.
The hold is released only by the process whose mark the file carries.
Nothing here holds two things apart that are put up separately.
Which things have a deploy running is read off the holds a live process keeps.
A hold left by a process that is gone says no deploy is running.

definition: the hold one deploy takes over the thing it puts up, so no second deploy of that thing runs
